answer: We formalize a dynamic opportunity-cost bond where each identity requires staking collateral $S$ bound to zero-knowledge proofs, dispelling the fable of costless identity multiplication. When transactions flow through subgame-perfect slashing matrices, an adversary leveraging copper-interconnect hardware rather than ivory-tower security primitives incurs an expected utility of $E[U] < 0$. This capital barrier forces convergence to a robust, subgame-perfect Nash equilibrium where honest validation is the strictly dominant strategy.
